# Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

## Summary
Read the plugin version at runtime from `packages/herdr/package.json` and render it as a dimmed, right-aligned `v<version>` suffix in the work item selection list header, without disturbing the left-aligned title.

## Acceptance Criteria
- A runtime helper reads the plugin version from `packages/herdr/package.json` (JSON parse via `readFileSync`, following the `shortcut-config.ts` pattern); when the file is missing or unparseable it falls back gracefully (e.g. `'?'` or omit) without throwing.
- The list-mode header renders `v<version>` right-aligned to `cols` (visible-width padding computed with ANSI codes stripped before padding), dimmed via `ANSI.dim`, matching the `[auto-refresh on]` treatment; the left-aligned `Work Items — N item(s)` title is unchanged.
- The version is read at runtime from the manifest, not hardcoded in the renderer (stays in sync with the manifest version).
- On narrow panes where the suffix would overlap the title, the suffix is dropped or truncated (guard on `cols`) — no layout breakage, no overflow beyond the pane width.
- Full project test suite passes with the new changes, including the header version tests (F1).

## Minimal Implementation
- Add a small version-read helper in `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts` (or a sibling module) using the `readFileSync`/`dirname` pattern from `shortcut-config.ts`, with a safe fallback.
- In the list-mode header renderer (near line ~1585): compute the header's visible width, pad to `cols`, and append the dimmed `v<version>` suffix right-aligned; reuse `truncateLine`/visible-length logic; guard on `cols` for narrow panes.
- Keep the renderer testable via the existing `readFile`-style injection seam where practical.

## Dependencies
- Blocked by: header version rendering tests (F1) — test-first ordering.

## Deliverables
- Updated `packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts`; version helper; no change to `packages/herdr/package.json` (version source only).
data.title: Implement version read + dimmed right-aligned header display

# Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal
When a work item with `priority=critical` transitions to a terminal state (status=completed or stage=in_review), automatically downgrade its priority to `high`.

## Implementation Details

### 1. Downgrade Logic

Add a helper function to detect and perform the auto-downgrade:
- Location: `packages/shared/src/database.ts` alongside the existing `cascadePriorityDowngrade`
- Function: `downgradeIfTerminal(item)` or inline check
- Logic: if item's new state has `status=completed` or `stage=in_review` AND `priority=critical`, set `priority=high`

### 2. Call Sites

Invoke from terminal-transition paths:
- `src/commands/update.ts` — after status/stage update, before response
- `src/commands/close.ts` — after close logic, before response

Prefer explicit call sites to avoid interfering with internal DB `update()` cascade calls.

### 3. Reporting

Report the downgrade in both output formats, mirroring the existing `downgradedChildren` pattern:
- JSON output: add `downgradedItem` field (or similar) with `{id, priority}` 
- Human-readable: add a summary line like `Downgraded priority from critical to high`

### 4. Constraints

- Only affect `critical` → `high` downgrade
- No change to other priorities (high/medium/low remain untouched)
- Only trigger on terminal transitions: `--status completed`, `--stage in_review`, or `wl close`
- Non-terminal transitions (e.g., `idea` → `plan_complete`) must NOT change priority

### Key Files
- `src/commands/update.ts` — terminal transition handling
- `src/commands/close.ts` — close path
- `packages/shared/src/database.ts` — helper function location
- `src/validators/priority.ts` — priority constants
data.title: Implement auto-downgrade of critical priority on terminal transitions

## Goal

Wire the hydrator into the worklist plugin (packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts) as a TaskScheduler task, visibility-gated, with an immediate run when the tab regains focus (reusing the existing resume-poll machinery). No second interval loop.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A scheduler task id 'hydrate' is registered on the existing TaskScheduler with intervalMs 30_000, singleFlight: true, and runTimeoutMs set; a rejecting task never takes down the scheduler loop.
2. The hydrate task is visibility-gated: while the worklist pane is hidden it does not run and spawns zero wl processes (paneGate pattern).
3. On a hidden→visible transition, hydration runs immediately (in addition to the existing refresh) without waiting for the next 30s tick.
4. Hydrator deps are injected into worklist.ts (e.g. via opts) so tests can substitute fakes.
5. Full project suite passes; no regressions in existing worklist tests.

- packages/herdr/src/worklist.ts — register hydrate task + resume hook
- packages/herdr/src/scheduler.ts — reused as-is
- packages/herdr/src/visibility.ts — reuse PollGate/paneGate
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — visibility-gated scheduler precedent

## Minimal Implementation

1. Register hydrate task alongside refresh/sync/resume-poll/downtime with the same interval/visibility wiring used by the downtime worker.
2. In the resume-poll hidden→visible transition branch, invoke the hydrate task immediately (parallel to the existing immediate refresh).

## Goal

Implement the herdr hydrator module (packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts): every 30s (and on worklist focus-resume) it fetches all in_progress work items, matches each against work-item IDs in active pane titles across all tabs of the current workspace, and demotes any item with no matching pane per the signal-based rule (AC3 of parent WL-0MSOJLZD9004P8PI). Pure decision functions + orchestration with injectable deps; fail-open at every boundary.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles(panes) returns WL-[0-9A-Z]+ IDs found in pane labels.
2. isActivePaneMatch(itemId, panes) returns true iff the ID appears in a running pane's label in any tab of the current workspace; workspace filtering via herdr pane list --workspace <id> / HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID env var.
3. decideDemotion(workItem, blockers): stage in_review → {status: completed, stage: in_review}; active outbound blocker (target not completed/deleted, stage not in_review/done, per isDependencyActive in packages/shared/src/database.ts) → {status: blocked, stage: plan_complete (or best compatible)}; else → {status: open, stage: intake_complete}; stage always chosen per src/config.ts compatibility.
4. runHydrationOnce(deps): fetches wl list --status in_progress, fetches panes, computes demotions, applies each via wl update (status+stage); an item with a matching pane is never touched.
5. Fail-open: wl/pane CLI missing, non-zero exit, or unparseable output → skip the entire cycle with a log; the function never throws; no demotion happens on untrustworthy evidence.
6. All hydrator.test.ts tests pass; full project suite passes.

## Key Files

- packages/herdr/src/hydrator.ts — new module
- packages/herdr/src/fetcher.ts — reuse runWl/extractJson/extractItems
- packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts — orchestration precedent
- src/commands/dep.ts + packages/shared/src/database.ts — dependency semantics (reference only)
- src/config.ts — status/stage compatibility (reference only)

## Minimal Implementation

1. Pure helpers: extractWorkItemIdsFromPaneTitles, isActivePaneMatch, decideDemotion (status, stage) pair.
2. runHydrationOnce(deps) with injectable {runWl, runPaneList, now, log}; fetch in_progress; fetch panes filtered to workspace; outbound-edge stage fetch per blocker candidate (wl dep list carries status only — fetch stage via wl show for each edge not completed/deleted).
3. Apply demotions; wrap whole cycle in try/catch that logs and returns without demoting.

## Dependencies

- Requires F1 (hydrator.test.ts — written first; suite must pass to close)
- Requires F0 (pane-title format amendment — ID must survive truncation)
data.title: Hydrator: demote stale in_progress items

data.description:
Discovered-from: WL-0MTV67MZU003H7SH.

When the audit runner runs child audits in separate-process mode (`--no-child-in-main-slot`), each child Phase-1 AC screen spawned a pi subprocess whose output could not be parsed: 'Warning: Unparseable Pi output for AC evaluation — falling back to partial verdict'. All child ACs were persisted as partial ('Ready to close: No'), which then reverted the in_review children to open/plan_complete and (via dependency reconciliation) to blocked — cascading a parent audit to 'Ready to close: No' even though the parent's own ACs were all met.

The default in-main-slot mode avoids this (child screens are performed by the invoking session), which is how the parent was ultimately verified green. Suggest: make separate-process child screening resilient to the local-proxy output format (or detect the unparseable case and retry/escalate instead of persisting partial), so the mode is usable in this environment.
data.title: Audit runner: separate-process child audits return unparseable pi output (falls back to partial)

Same latent hermeticity defect as WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI, found while fixing it: several worklist test files match herdr CLI calls with `bin === 'herdr'`. Because `isPaneVisible()` / pane helpers resolve the CLI as `process.env.HERDR_BIN_PATH ?? 'herdr'`, those mocks silently miss whenever the suite runs inside a herdr pane (which sets HERDR_BIN_PATH to an absolute path), and the call falls through to the mock's generic branch — which can flip a visibility probe to fail-open 'visible'.

Verified call sites (argument-based matching is the fix): packages/herdr/src/worklist-agent-state-event.test.ts:114, worklist-agent-state.test.ts:78, worklist-expand-refresh.test.ts:121,200, worklist-icons.test.ts:89, worklist-inflight.test.ts:102, worklist-nested-expand.test.ts:128, fetcher-timeout.test.ts:113,374.

Currently non-blocking: the full suite is green (the affected assertions do not depend on the missed branch), so this is hardening, not a live failure. Discovered from: WL-0MU2FM1L60002URI.
data.title: Harden remaining exec mocks against HERDR_BIN_PATH (match herdr calls by args, not binary name)

# Intake Brief — wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills (WL-0MUAD8U24001ZK5K)

## Problem statement

The `refactor` and `standup` skills read and (for refactor) create worklog data, but neither begins by pulling remote worklog changes. A stale local SQLite store can therefore produce duplicate `REFACTOR` work items, stale standup reports, and un-pushed local changes. The requested behaviour is that **`wl sync` runs as the first action** of both skills, before any other worklog interaction.

## Users

- **Agents invoking `/skill:refactor` or `/skill:standup`** — they need current worklog data so analysis and reporting are based on the same state the operator sees.
  - *As an agent, I want refactor/standup to sync first, so I never file duplicate smells or report stale items.*
- **Operators reading standup reports** — the report must reflect the actual remote queue.
  - *As an operator, I want my standup to reflect synced data, so it drives the right priorities.*
- **Producers reviewing refactor-filed work items** — fewer duplicate `REFACTOR` items to triage.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `/skill:refactor` (both the no-ID full-project scan and the `<id>` session-only mode) performs `wl sync` as the **first worklog operation**, before any work-item read, comment injection, or work-item creation. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
2. `/skill:standup` performs `wl sync` before its first `wl next` / `wl list` fetch. Verified by an automated test asserting call ordering.
3. The sync invocation is **lock-aware** (uses `wl sync --if-idle`) and single-flight, so overlapping or concurrent invocations skip rather than block or pile up. Verified by a test asserting the `--if-idle` argument / skip behaviour.
4. A **failed sync is non-fatal**: offline, unborn-HEAD, author-gate, or lock-contention failures log a warning and the skill continues with local data, preserving its existing exit-code semantics. Verified by a test that stubs a failing sync and asserts the skill still proceeds.
5. Both `SKILL.md` files document that `wl sync` runs first, what happens on failure, and how to disable it for offline/deterministic runs (`--no-sync`).
6. A `--no-sync` escape hatch (or equivalent injectable runner) exists so tests and offline runs never perform a real network sync; the existing test suites remain hermetic.
7. When no `.worklog` context is resolvable, sync is skipped gracefully rather than erroring.
8. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
9. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Target repository:** the `refactor` and `standup` skills are maintained in the **SorraAgents agent-framework repo** (`/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/...`). This work item is tracked in the **ContextHub** worklog; see Open Questions — implementation location must be confirmed before the implement workflow can run.
- Sync must be bounded and non-interactive; it must never hang an agent session.
- No new third-party dependencies.
- Reuse the existing `wl` CLI and the shared `run_wl` helper (`skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py`) rather than shelling out ad hoc; a single shared helper should serve both skills to avoid divergence.
- Must not change refactor scan/detection semantics or standup report content/format.
- Respect repo ignore rules and the author-gate behaviour of `wl sync` (do not add `--allow-foreign-author`).

## Existing state

- **No skill currently runs `wl sync`.** A search of `skill/**/scripts/*.py` for sync calls returns none (only the `wl` CLI itself and the ContextHub herdr auto-sync).
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` exposes `run_wl(cmd)`, which injects `--worklog-dir` with prefix/cwd resolution — the natural wrapper for a shared `sync_worklog()` helper.
- `wl sync` supports `--if-idle` ("Skip (exit 0) if another sync is already in progress — lock-aware guard for auto-sync spawners"), `--no-push`, `--worklog-dir`, and `--json`.
- ContextHub's `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts` already implements the `--if-idle` fire-and-forget pattern (single-flight guard + heartbeat freshness) — a proven precedent for non-blocking, non-fatal sync.
- `refactor.py` entry point: `main()` → `_build_pipeline_runner()` → pipeline; session mode wraps `StatusLifecycle(restore_on_exit=True)`.
- `generate_standup.py` entry point: `main()` resolves `--worklog-dir` then calls `generate_report()` which performs the `wl next` / `wl list` fetches via `fetch_json`.
- Existing tests: `skill/standup/tests/` (3 files: default output path, worklog-dir, regressions). Refactor has no dedicated test package in the skill tree.

## Desired change

1. Add a shared helper (e.g. `skill/shared/worklog_sync.py`) that runs `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl`, returns success/skip status, and never raises on failure.
2. Invoke it as the first action in both `refactor.py` and `generate_standup.py`, before any other `wl` call.
3. Add `--no-sync` to both scripts and thread it through so tests/offline runs skip syncing.
4. Update both `SKILL.md` files to state sync-first behaviour and the `--no-sync` flag.
5. Add focused tests for ordering, `--if-idle`, failure tolerance, and `--no-sync`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/scripts/refactor.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper before the pipeline in `main()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/scripts/generate_standup.py` — invoke shared sync-first helper in `main()` before `generate_report()`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/shared/worklog_sync.py` — **new** shared helper wrapping `wl sync --if-idle` via `run_wl` (fail-soft).
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — document sync-first + `--no-sync`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/SKILL.md` — document sync-first + `--no-sync`.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/standup/tests/test_generate_standup_sync_first.py` — **new** ordering / failure / `--no-sync` tests.
- `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/skill/refactor/tests/test_refactor_sync_first.py` — **new** ordering / failure / `--no-sync` tests.

## Related work

- **ContextHub `packages/herdr/src/auto-sync.ts`** — existing `wl sync --if-idle` single-flight/heartbeat implementation; reuse its semantics/guard pattern (see WL-0MSGAEJQA005QG3W heartbeat, WL-0MT50S9JW001DHME dispatch parallelism).
- **WL-0MTK1ILM2009QYB2** — *Dispatcher consumes Herdr selection list head* — standup's data source/ranking is anchored to the Herdr selection list; sync-first affects the freshness of that input.
- **SA-0MTSNTZOV006P79V** — *Refactor skill should run immediately when invoked without an ID* — established the refactor invocation convention; the sync-first step must fit inside it without adding prompts.
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX / SA-0MSGH57JL001OZER** — recent `wl sync` robustness work (identity gate; no-commit repos) — informs the failure-tolerance AC.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** "all worklog-reading skills should sync first" is a tempting generalisation. **Mitigation:** scope strictly to `refactor` and `standup`; track a generalisation as a separate work item if desired.
- **Latency/lock-contention risk:** an unconditional blocking sync could stall agent sessions. **Mitigation:** `--if-idle`, bounded/non-interactive invocation, non-fatal on failure.
- **Hermetic-test risk:** real syncs in CI would hit the network/author gate. **Mitigation:** injectable runner + `--no-sync`, asserted in tests.
- **Cross-repo risk:** the code lives in SorraAgents while the work item is in ContextHub; the implement workflow's worktree is repo-scoped. **Mitigation:** producer decision on work-item placement (Open Question 1).
- **Assumption:** "first thing run" means the first *worklog operation* — argument parsing, help, and `--worklog-dir` resolution may precede it.
- **Assumption:** sync failure should not abort the skill (read-only/analysis workflows should still produce output from local data).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **OPEN QUESTION 1 — Repository / worklog ownership.** The `refactor` and `standup` skills live in the **SorraAgents** repo (`SorraAgents/skill/...`), but this item is in the **ContextHub** worklog (WL-). The implement workflow creates a worktree in the work-item's repo and refuses changes outside it, so the target repo must be explicit. **Recommended:** implement in SorraAgents under a linked SA work item (agent-framework is the canonical skills home), with this WL item recording the requirement and cross-referencing it. — Awaiting producer.
- **OPEN QUESTION 2 — Where should the sync run?** (A) In the scripts (`refactor.py`, `generate_standup.py`) as the first executable step; (B) only as prose in `SKILL.md` for the agent to run. **Recommended:** (A) — deterministic and testable — plus documented in `SKILL.md`. — Awaiting producer.
- **OPEN QUESTION 3 — Failure and concurrency semantics.** Should a failed sync abort the skill or warn-and-continue? Should the sync use `--if-idle`? And should a `--no-sync` escape hatch exist for tests/offline? **Recommended:** warn-and-continue, `--if-idle`, and a `--no-sync` flag — Awaiting producer.
data.title: wl sync to be run before refactor and standup skills

## Summary

`test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is a **test artifact** created and deleted by `test/migrations.test.ts` (its `beforeEach` unlinks the DB and clears the dir), but it is tracked in git and not gitignored. Every full-suite run rewrites it, so `implement.py finish` (which commits all worktree changes) includes a meaningless binary diff in the implementation commit.

Observed while implementing **WL-0MUEBQLRD00288VV**: commit `ab2fb518` includes `test/tmp_mig/worklog.db | Bin 36864 -> 36864 bytes`; previous commits `cfdb9651` and `f19c74b6` carry the same churn.

- `test/tmp_mig/` (or at least the generated `worklog.db`) is not tracked; add it to `.gitignore` and `git rm --cached` the existing file.
- Optionally have `test/migrations.test.ts` use an OS temp dir (like `tests/` does with `createTempDir()`) so it never writes inside the repo.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `test/tmp_mig/worklog.db` is no longer tracked and `test/tmp_mig/` is gitignored.
2. Running the full suite leaves `git status` clean (no binary churn).

## Goal

Create a pure filter function that checks whether a non-terminal cooldown
applies to an item+kind pair, based on the rolling pane-close log.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Function `isNonTerminalCooldownActive` in `downtime-log.ts`:
   - Reads `entryType: "pane-close"` entries from the passed entries array
   - Non-terminal reason codes: anything except `"none"` (e.g. `agent-ended-no-terminal`, `audit-ended-no-result`, `producer-review`, `risk-effort-incomplete`, `reached-in-review`)
   - Terminal outcomes have `reasonCode: "none"` - they do NOT trigger cooldown
   - Returns true when: a non-terminal close for the same itemId+kind exists AND cooldownMs has NOT elapsed since the close timestamp
   - Returns false when: no close record, or the close is older than cooldownMs, or the close was terminal
   - Fail-closed: missing/unparseable timestamp returns true (skip dispatch)

2. Stage advancement releases (AC4 of parent):
   - The function receives itemStage (current worklog stage of the item)
   - If the current stage rank is HIGHER than the dispatched-at stage rank, return false (released)
   - Stage rank ordering: idea=0, intake_complete=1, plan_complete=2, in_review=3

3. Tests: Unit tests covering:
   - (a) non-terminal close then immediate idle returns true (skip)
   - (b) close older than cooldownMs returns false (eligible)
   - (c) stage advancement mid-cooldown returns false (eligible)
   - (d) terminal success reasonCode equals none returns false (eligible)
   - (e) missing/unparseable close timestamp returns true (fail-closed skip)
data.title: Create non-terminal cooldown filter function

## Goal

Wire the non-terminal cooldown filter into both the Herdr-list-head path

## Feature 3: Implement core pane-triage logic (enumerate, classify, report)

### Summary
Implement the core Python module: workspace resolution, pane enumeration via shelling out to the reaper CLI `--json` mode, report rendering (Idle/Active tables, log tails, recommendation rules), and the approval-gated close flow.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `resolve_workspace()` returns the workspace from `HERDR_WORKSPACE_ID` or falls back to `herdr pane current`; reports only that workspace.
2. `enumerate_and_classify()` shells out to the reaper CLI (`--json`), parses the JSON output, and enriches each pane with work-item context. The item id is derived from the shared `paneItemIdFromLabel` (exposed in the reaper JSON), not re-parsed in Python. The `needsProducerReview` value is obtained via `wl show <id> --json` for the parsed item id.
3. `build_report()` renders Idle and Active tables (tab, title, pane id) and, for idle items, the work item id and `needsProducerReview` value. **Idle** specifically means the shared classifier's reasonCode is `'marker'` (the `</end_session>` marker is present at the end of the final assistant message), per parent AC2.
4. Each idle item's last 20 log lines are printed under the heading `<pane title> Needs Review <true|false>`.
5. Recommendation rules: the "Recommended to close" table excludes the invoking pane (`HERDR_PANE_ID`) and panes with `needsProducerReview=true`. Additionally, panes with reasonCode `implement` or `live-children` (inherited from the shared classifier's never-close guards) are also excluded.
6. Re-verify-before-close: re-reads `herdr pane list` immediately before each close; any pane that became active is skipped with a reason in the Closed ledger.

### Constraints
- Shared classifier is mandatory: consume idle classification from the ContextHub reaper CLI (`--json`), never re-implement the `</end_session>` check.
- Never-close guards are universal (per producer Q-OPEN-2): `needsProducerReview=true` panes are never closed, by manual skill or automatic reaper. `implement` panes and panes with live child processes are also excluded (inherited from the shared classifier).
- Workspace-scoped only — no cross-workspace roll-up.
- Fail-closed on herdr CLI errors: clear message, no partial mutation.

### Deliverables
- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` (full implementation)

## Feature 4: Approval prompt and closure ledger

### Summary
Implement the approval gate and the per-pane closure ledger for the pane-triage skill.

### Acceptance Criteria
1. `prompt_approval()` blocks for producer input with the options: `yes` (close all recommended), `select` (choose specific panes), `no` (close none).
2. `no` or ambiguous input closes nothing; the invoking pane is never closed.
3. On `yes`/`select`, approved panes are closed one-by-one with a re-verify step between each (see Feature 3 AC6).
4. A Closed ledger records, per pane: pane id, title, status (closed/skipped), and a reason for skips.
5. The ledger is printed at the end of the run.

### Constraints
- The approval gate is mandatory — the skill never closes anything unattended.
- No pane is closed without explicit producer approval.

### Deliverables
- `SorraAgents/skill/pane-triage/scripts/pane_triage.py` (approval + ledger additions)

# Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close

## Problem statement

Mechanism A (the scheduled reaper, `pane-close.ts::classifySession`) has two
classification bugs and should be re-enabled once they are fixed:

1. `!agentProcessAlive` (step 6) currently closes the pane (`dead-agent`).
   A dead agent does not mean the pane is safe to close — the operator may
   still need to read the final output. This should be **no close**.
2. The idle timeout (step 7) only supports a positive threshold. It should
   accept `<= 0` meaning **never close on idle**, with a **default of `0`**
   (idle-based closing disabled by default).

With the idle default at `0`, the auto-close feature can be safely re-enabled
via `paneCloseEnabled` (currently `false`).

## Background

- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — created the pane-lifecycle classifier.
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper.
- **WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC** — parent improvement item for pane auto-close.
- Mechanism A was disabled by default (`paneCloseEnabled: false`) pending
  classification fixes; this item covers the fixes needed to re-enable it.

## Current behaviour

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts::classifySession` — step 6 returns
  `{ close: true, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }` when `!agentProcessAlive`.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — `DEFAULT_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 * 60 * 1000`
  (30 minutes); no `<= 0` handling.
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = false`,
  `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 30`.
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — `paneCloseEnabled`, `paneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes`.

## Desired change

- Dead-agent path returns `{ close: false, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }`.
- Idle threshold `<= 0` returns `{ close: false }` (never close on idle),
  with `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES = 0`.
- `clampPaneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes` must permit `0` (so the minimum range
  becomes `0..1440`, and the scheduler must not coerce `0` back to a positive
  default).
- `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED = true` to re-enable Mechanism A auto-close.
- Update the classifier doc comment to reflect the new outcome ordering.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — Dead agent does not close.** `classifySession` returns
   `{ close: false, reasonCode: 'dead-agent' }` when `agentProcessAlive` is
   `false` (and no higher-precedence guard/close applies).
2. **AC2 — Idle `<= 0` never closes.** With `idleThresholdMs <= 0`,
   `classifySession` never returns a close decision via the `idle-threshold`
   path, regardless of `idleMs`.
3. **AC3 — Default idle threshold is 0.** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_IDLE_THRESHOLD_MINUTES`
   is `0` and `clampPaneCloseIdleThresholdMinutes` accepts `0`.
4. **AC4 — Auto-close re-enabled.** `DEFAULT_PANE_CLOSE_ENABLED` is `true`,
   so the scheduled reaper runs by default.
5. **AC5 — Tests.** Table-driven tests cover the dead-agent no-close path and
   the `<= 0` idle-threshold no-close path (including negative tests proving
   the previous false-positive closes no longer occur).
6. **AC6 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
7. **AC7 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.ts` — Classification logic and default threshold
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.ts` — Defaults and clamping
- `packages/herdr/src/settings.ts` — Configuration options
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close.test.ts` — Classifier tests
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-close-scheduler.test.ts` — Scheduler tests

## Related work

- WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic (parent)
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — pane-lifecycle classifier origin
- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — pane-close scheduler/reaper origin

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should the dead-agent path do?" — Answer (operator):
  "should be no close". Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "What should the idle timeout default and `<= 0` semantics be?" —
  Answer (operator): "should allow a value of <=0 which means never close on
  idle. This should be set to a default of 0." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Should auto-close be re-enabled?" — Answer (operator): "Then re-enable
  autoclose via mechanism A". Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Improve Mechanism A idle timeout algorithm and re-enable auto-close

# Reconsider and disable Mechanism B (dispatch-monitor) pane auto-close

## Problem statement

Mechanism B (`packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts::classifyPaneLifecycle`),
driven from the downtime worker's dispatch monitor, is not working well and is
being **disabled** while the scheduled reaper (Mechanism A) is re-enabled.
Mechanism B needs to be revisited and either fixed or replaced.

## Background

- **WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC** — parent improvement item for pane auto-close.
- **WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN** — created the pane-lifecycle classifier (Mechanism B).
- **WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS** — established the pane-close scheduler and reaper
  (Mechanism A).
- **WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI** — fixes Mechanism A and re-enables it.

There are two independent classifiers today:

- **Mechanism A** — `pane-close.ts::classifySession`, run by the scheduled
  reaper. Session-state based (marker / dead agent / idle) with explicit
  never-close guards.
- **Mechanism B** — `pane-lifecycle.ts::classifyPaneLifecycle`, run from the
  downtime worker against the rolling dispatch log. Worklog-stage based.

Mechanism B has been observed to close panes prematurely and to race with
Mechanism A (no shared atomic lock; both check idempotency non-atomically).
With Mechanism A re-enabled and improved, Mechanism B should be switched off
and its design reconsidered rather than left running.

## Current behaviour

- The worker invokes `classifyPaneLifecycle` (see `downtime-worker.ts` around
  the pane-lifecycle pass) and closes panes for every non-`implement` kind,
  including `requires-attention` outcomes.
- Mechanisms A and B use different classifiers and share only a
  non-atomic `alreadyClosedPaneIds` / log-key idempotency set.

## Desired change (this item)

1. Disable Mechanism B's pane-closing behaviour so it does not run.
2. Add an explicit code comment at the Mechanism B call site / module header
   stating that this mechanism is disabled because it is not working well and
   needs to be revisited (with a reference to this work item).
3. Capture the analysis of why Mechanism B misbehaves (stage-propagation lag,
   `requires-attention` still closing, races with Mechanism A) so a future
   session can decide whether to fix, replace, or delete it.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **AC1 — Mechanism B disabled.** The dispatch-monitor pane-close path is
   switched off and does not close panes; Mechanism A remains the only active
   auto-close path.
2. **AC2 — Explicit code comment.** A clear comment in the relevant source
   (module header and/or call site) states that Mechanism B is disabled
   because it is not working well and needs to be revisited, referencing this
   work item.
3. **AC3 — Tests.** Tests assert Mechanism B no longer closes panes (or is not
   invoked) while Mechanism A continues to function; existing Mechanism B unit
   tests are retained but clearly marked as covering disabled behaviour.
4. **AC4 — Docs.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
   changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs
   site entries.
5. **AC5 — Full suite.** Full project test suite must pass with the new
   changes.

## Key files

- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.ts` — Mechanism B classifier (comment / disable)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — Mechanism B call site
- `packages/herdr/src/pane-lifecycle.test.ts` — Mechanism B tests

## Related work

- WL-0MUMCZAC40058HCC — Improve pane auto-close logic (parent)
- WL-0MUMEJHT9004EQPI — Improve Mechanism A and re-enable auto-close
- WL-0MU308WSF0002JWN — pane-lifecycle classifier origin
- WL-0MUJL1NAH0042GOS — pane-close scheduler/reaper origin

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "What should happen to Mechanism B?" — Answer (operator): "Leave
  mechanism B disabled and comment in the code to make it clear this is not
  working well and needs to be revisited. Create a work item to reconsider
  this mechanism." Source: interactive reply.
data.title: Reconsider and disable Mechanism B (dispatch-monitor) pane auto-close
